blocking.problem: The subtraction rule says only “the same with sub and borrows icmp ult a_k, b_k” after the addition recurrence, which includes v_k = icmp ult m_k,t_k and c_k = u_k OR v_k. Replacing add by sub and changing the first comparison to a_k<b_k leaves the incoming-borrow test wrong: underflow in t_k-borrow makes m_k greater than t_k. Concrete i192 witness, low limb first: a=[0,1,1]=2^128+2^64, b=[1,1,0]=2^64+1. Limb 0 borrows; limb 1 has t_1=0 and incoming borrow 1, giving m_1=0xffffffffffffffff. Both a_1<b_1 and inherited m_1<t_1 are false, incorrectly clearing the borrow into limb 2. This expansion yields [0xffffffffffffffff,0xffffffffffffffff,1]=2^129-1 rather than [0xffffffffffffffff,0xffffffffffffffff,0]=2^128-1. If “borrows” is intended to replace more comparisons, those replacements are unstated and the two readings diverge. LLVM 18 and 23 instcombine independently fold the source to 340282366920938463463374607431768211455 and the inherited-comparison expansion to 680564733841876926926749214863536422911. This is a result error, not a proof-format gap.
blocking.fix: Replace the section 12.7 subtraction bullet with: “Let beta_-1=0. At limb k of width w_k compute t_k=a_k-b_k modulo 2^w_k; z_k is the zero-extended incoming beta_(k-1), using identity conversion when w_k=1; m_k=t_k-z_k modulo 2^w_k. When another limb follows, beta_k=(icmp ult a_k,b_k) OR (icmp ult t_k,z_k). Discard the final outgoing borrow for wrapping subtraction.” Do not inherit addition’s m_k<t_k comparison. Add a checked normalisation/native vector sub i192 (2^128+2^64),(2^64+1), expecting [0xffffffffffffffff,0xffffffffffffffff,0] and code 0. A single comparison at width w_k+1 against b_k+beta_(k-1) is also viable; I recommend the two-stage recurrence because it matches the current expansion and avoids wrapping that sum.

blocking.section: 16.4 getelementptr row; 17.4 CC/R lowering; 18.1 C state
blocking.problem: Section 16.4 sign-extends/truncates every GEP index to pw, takes constant offsets modulo 2^pw, and performs full-width pointer addition. LLVM datalayout separately specifies pointer representation width and pointer index width; GEP uses the latter. No dialect verdict rule excludes their differing. Witness materialised function under datalayout “e-p:64:64:64:32”: define i64 @f(i64 %i) { %p = inttoptr i64 4294967296 to ptr; %q = getelementptr i8, ptr %p, i64 %i; %r = ptrtoint ptr %q to i64; ret i64 %r }. At i=4294967296 the 32-bit GEP offset is zero, so f returns 4294967296. The pw=64 map returns 8589934592. Neither path accesses memory or faults; non-inbounds pointer arithmetic is defined. Both LLVM 18 and 23 fold a constant instantiation of the source to 4294967296 and its mapped addition to 8589934592. The dynamic-index form can reach materialisation through the supported O0 envelope. Thus the LangRef state of section 18.1 and the section 16.4 reference object compute different functions.
blocking.fix: Replace section 16.4’s GEP rule with: “Let I be the datalayout pointer-index width for the base pointer address space, defaulting to pointer width when omitted. Sign-extend or truncate each sequential index to I. Compute scaled indices, structure offsets and accumulated byte offsets modulo 2^I using datalayout allocation sizes. Add the offset to the low I bits of the base modulo 2^I, preserving base bits above I unchanged, and reassemble the pointer carrier. Apply this rule also to constant-expression GEPs and to CC/R lowering in section 17.4.” I=pw reduces to the current arithmetic. Add the witness above with input/output 4294967296 and code 0, plus an offset-wrap vector. Normalising GEP into explicit integer operations before mapping is another viable implementation; I recommend specifying the map semantics and sharing it with CC/R, without introducing a layout rejection.
